title: add-load-diffusion-prober-and-smooth-fallback-oracle
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: production rollouts occasionally experienced sharp, short-duration latency spikes when traffic shifts concentrated on a small set of worker shards. This PR introduces a traffic-aware Load Diffusion Prober and a Smooth Fallback Oracle to reduce false-positive rollbacks and provide graceful stall protection during bursty traffic. The Load Diffusion Prober continuously samples routing keys and estimates effective shard utilization and collision probability; when hotspots are detected it adjusts probe weights and issues soft-penalties instead of hard rollbacks. The Smooth Fallback Oracle consumes prober signals plus percentile-residual smoothing to decide fallback windows and maximum rollback budgets. Implementation: - lightweight prober module with opt-in sampling policy tied to rollout gates - reservoir-based diffusion estimator that adapts window size by observed burstiness - percentile residual smoother (EMA over 99th/95th) to avoid reacting to single-bucket spikes - integration layer with existing canary-evaluator and rollout-controller - feature flag and config knobs for dedicated vs shared pools Tests & validation: unit and integration tests for estimator math, simulations with synthetic burst traces, and a 48-hour production shadow run on staging showing 60% fewer unnecessary rollbacks and 30% lower 99th latency amplification during traffic bursts. Backwards compatibility: defaults are off; existing rollout logic remains unchanged unless feature flag enabled. Related: ENG-2381 (reduce noisy rollbacks), ENG-2399 (improve burst resilience). Checklist: [x] design doc linked [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] staging shadow run [x] dashboard and alert updates [x] docs update (console UI config).

review_comments: Priya Menon: Nice design. Two high-level asks: 1) add a short doc string describing failure modes the smoother might mask, 2) include a guard that prevents fallback during capacity-constrained windows.
Ethan Park: Responded - added doc strings and a config knob (max_fallback_budget) to the rollout_adapter and updated defaults.yaml. Also added a unit test for the guard behavior.
Carlos Alvarez: Left a small comment on reservoir edge-case when sample rate is very low; suggested a min-window floor.
Ethan Park: Added min_window=5s floor and noted trade-offs in code comments. Pushed follow-up commit.
Tala Jensen: Approve after CI green. Verified dashboard tile visuals in staging and shadow metrics look sane.
merge_summary: Squash merged by Priya Menon after green CI and two approvals. Feature gated by 'enable_load_diffusion' flag; rollout requires a minimum sample rate and operator enablement.
release_notes: Add: Load Diffusion Prober and Smooth Fallback Oracle to reduce noisy rollbacks during bursty traffic. Opt-in feature behind configuration flag. Safe defaults unchanged.
notes_for_ops: Enable behind canary.feature_flags.enable_load_diffusion with conservative defaults first (sample_rate=0.01, min_window=5s, max_fallback_budget=0.2). Monitor canary.rollback_count and latency_residuals for first 72h.
perf_summary: Staging shadow run (48h, synthetic burst traces) results: - unnecessary rollback rate down 60% - 99th-latency amplification during bursts reduced by ~30% - no impact to median latency
